items.title: Predictive Risk Scores in the Public Sector: Experimental Evidence from Child-Protection Investigations
items.desc: A randomized evaluation of 4,752 child-protection referrals finds that giving supervisors an algorithmic risk score raised foster-care placements and services for the highest-risk children, cut later maltreatment referrals, and showed no evidence of widening racial disparities. [NBER, posted 2026-08-03]

items.title: Navigating the skill diversity frontier: How skill complexity explains worker resilience
items.desc: As AI reshapes labor markets, the authors build a measure of how the structure and complexity of a worker's skill portfolio shapes resilience to technological change, moving beyond occupation or credential-based views of human capital. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-08-03]

items.title: AI Governance for Institutional Readiness in Finance
items.desc: A survey finds 88% of finance professionals report no operational governance framework for agentic AI despite universal awareness of its use, and only 24 of 75 large U.S. money managers disclosing AI in Form ADV filings have a formal policy; the authors argue the gap is architectural and propose governance design. [arXiv econ.EM/q-fin.RM, posted 2026-08-03]

items.title: AI Financial Advice: Supply, Demand, and Life Cycle Implications
items.desc: Using prompts written by a representative sample and simulating lifetime outcomes of following GPT-5.2's spending and investing advice, the study finds the advice would push people toward life-cycle theory: broader diversified-equity participation and age-declining equity shares. [arXiv econ.GN/q-fin.PM, posted 2026-08-03]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: How China gets better bang for its buck than America in AI
items.desc: The Economist examines why China appears to extract more economic return per dollar of AI investment than the United States, and what that gap implies for the two countries' AI-driven growth. [Economist, 2026-08-03]

items.title: I Helped Run Lululemon. Companies Need to Stop Kidding Themselves About A.I.
items.desc: A former Lululemon executive argues that firms are overstating near-term AI productivity gains and using AI as cover for layoffs, warning that the hype is outrunning what the technology actually delivers in operations. [NYT opinion, 2026-08-03]

items.title: White House Whipsaws Silicon Valley (and Itself) Over A.I. Rules
items.desc: An account of shifting and contradictory federal signals on AI regulation, and how the resulting policy uncertainty is complicating investment and planning for tech firms. [NYT, 2026-08-04]

items.title: One chart shows the incredible reversal at American tech companies
items.desc: The Washington Post shows how heavy AI capital spending by leading U.S. firms is burning through cash, marking a sharp reversal from the sector's historically strong free-cash-flow position. [Washington Post, 2026-08-03]
